standard_prerequisites.name: The resolution criterion for complexes over a ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: More on Algebra, the remark listing the three conditions sufficient for a property of complexes to hold for all K, together with Derived Categories, the lemma comparing exact functors on triangles
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies conditions (2) and (3) of the criterion and its conclusion.

core_obligations: Set up the criterion (proof lines 20175-20180): the canonical map goes from right to left; let T(K) be the property that the displayed identity holds, and check the three conditions of the resolution criterion.
Check (1) (proof lines 20181-20184): both sides commute with direct sums because cd(X) is finite, which is the finite-cohomological-dimension lemma.

Check (2) and (3) (proof lines 20185-20190): condition (2) holds because both sides are exact functors of K between triangulated categories and the triangle criterion applies, and condition (3) is the obvious case K = Lambda[k], so the criterion gives the statement for all K.
proof_roadmap: Formulate the statement as a property T of the complex K and invoke the three-condition resolution criterion.
Verify commutation with direct sums from finite cohomological dimension.
Verify the exactness condition by the triangle criterion and the base case K = Lambda[k].
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes global sections after tensoring with a constant complex over a torsion ring on a scheme of finite cohomological dimension (statement lines 20163-20172). The proof (proof lines 20174-20190) verifies the three hypotheses of the resolution criterion: commutation with direct sums from finite cohomological dimension, the exactness condition through the triangle criterion, and the base case K = Lambda[k]. H2: one criterion applied with three short verifications.
